## About the course

How can a well-crafted cyberattack disrupt a physical system, a power grid for instance, while remaining undetected by its operator for long enough to do damage? The course answers with the tools of system theory, in four steps:

- **Introduction:** what a cyber-physical system is, the power system as the reference example, the attacks that have actually happened, and risk management as the framework that organizes every activity of cyber-physical security.
- **Modelling:** the networked cyber-physical system (plant, controller, detector, communication network, attacker), the attack space of the adversary, and the conditions under which an attack cannot be detected or identified.
- **Attacks:** the most important attack schemes, from static to dynamical ones, modelled and analysed one by one: false data injection against state estimation, topology and load redistribution attacks, load altering and switching attacks, zero dynamics attacks, covert attacks, replay and denial of service.
- **Defence:** detectors and observers, watermarking, secure control allocation, encrypted control, resilient control, and the optimal allocation of protection measures.

At the end of the course the student is able to model an attack and its physical effect on the system, to tell in which cases the attack can remain undetected, and to design detectors and defence strategies. The same knowledge serves in practice for vulnerability assessment and for designing systems that are more resilient to attacks. Most of the concepts are demonstrated through simulations in Julia and Matlab. See the [program](program.qmd) and the [schedule](schedule.qmd).

**Prerequisites:** fundamentals of mathematical analysis (derivatives, integrals, differential equations), linear algebra (linear systems, matrices, determinant, rank) and physics (elementary circuits and mechanical systems). The system theory needed, such as state space models, their solution and stability, is introduced during the course when it is needed, so that the course is accessible also to students coming from cybersecurity.
